first_findings.issue: Unsigned lexical spelling alone permits a byte-capped but very long integer. json_value delegates parse_int to the Python runtime, whose conversion limit and cost are not frozen by the proposal. A preconversion integer-token resource limit is missing.
first_findings.action: Freeze a named finite digit ceiling and bounded refusal before json_value/int conversion. Every valid pinned Body integer field fits a small finite token length; keep the additional resource ceiling explicit and distinguish it from malformed integer spelling. Include boundary and just-over-bound raw literal recipes. Co-reviewer proposes a twenty-digit resource ceiling and INPUT_INTEGER_BOUND/PREPARSE; sole owner must adopt exact semantics before coding. No valid Body integer maximum may be silently reduced.

first_findings.issue: Proposal permits direct fullmatch for the three pinned patterns, but JSON Schema pattern matching uses search semantics. The pinned Id and Base64 patterns use dollar end anchors that can match before a final newline. Thus Id A followed by LF and Base64 AAAA followed by LF match the pinned patterns under search but not fullmatch.
first_findings.observed_check: Standard-library re.search returned true and re.fullmatch returned false for both exact pinned patterns and those literal strings. This tests pattern semantics only, not the proposed component.
first_findings.action: For this shape-only increment use exact fixed-pattern search semantics and separately apply explicitly frozen protocol byte/identifier/base64 rules. Alternatively retain a separately named stronger protocol gate with its own controls; never report stricter fullmatch as identical pinned-schema behavior. Do not change the pinned schema silently.

Existing json_value enforces byte cap, duplicate decoded object-key detection, depth preflight, strict UTF-8 decode and parser rejection of float/constants. It does not itself reject negative integer spellings or escaped unpaired Unicode surrogates.

A paired surrogate escape may decode to a scalar but remains noncanonical compared with literal UTF-8; an unpaired surrogate must refuse encoding before canonical serialization. Canonical UTF-8 equality alone is too late to satisfy an explicit preparse scalar gate.
